timecoda

timecoda is an R package for implementing current methods of time-use epidemiology, in particular compositional data analysis applied to behavioural data.

The framework behind the package comes from a series of publications. Together they set out the definitions, concepts, statistical methods and research areas of time-use epidemiology (Pedišić, 2014; Pedišić et al., 2017; Dumuid, Stanford, Martín-Fernández, et al., 2018; Dumuid, Stanford, Pedišić, et al., 2018; Dumuid et al., 2019, 2020). For further information on the topic, see the International Network of Time-Use Epidemiologists (INTUE).

Installation

timecoda needs R 4.4.0 or newer. To install it from GitHub, use the pak package:

install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("MarcusVVLopes/timecoda")

To install all the suggested packages for optional features, run the same call with dependencies = TRUE.

pak::pak("MarcusVVLopes/timecoda", dependencies = TRUE)

Getting help and contributing

To ask a question or report a bug, use the issue tracker. Before you write any code for a new feature, discuss it in an issue. For instructions on proposing a change, see the contributing guide, and follow the code of conduct when you contribute.

Development

The developers specify the statistical methods and write the first implementation of each feature. Before release, each statistical method is benchmarked against established R packages (such as robCompositions, compositions and codaredistlm), hand-fitted models or published results. These benchmarks are part of the package’s tests (tests/testthat/test-benchmark-*.R), so anyone can rerun them.

AI tools (Claude, by Anthropic) help with documentation, tests, code review and refactoring. The developers review everything these tools produce and remain responsible for the package.

Citation

To cite timecoda, run citation("timecoda"):

Lopes MVV, Tozetto WR, de Camargo R, Zhang K (2026). timecoda: Compositional Data Analysis for Time-Use Behaviour Research. R package version 0.6.0, https://github.com/MarcusVVLopes/timecoda.
